Tableau

Turn complex data into questions a team can explore.

TOfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Tableau supports interactive visual analysis over connected data sources. We can design dashboards that let a team examine performance by channel, market, product, or customer cohort without losing the agreed metric definitions. The work includes the data model, useful filters, clear labels, and drill-down views so an executive question can lead to a specific operational decision.

Useful outputs

  • Interactive workbook and drill-down views
  • Documented calculation and filter logic
  • Refresh, sharing, and access configuration

Where we can apply it

  • Commercial scorecard: modeled sales → channel comparison → opportunity drill-down.
  • Cohort analysis: customer history → cohort definition → retention exploration.
  • Operations review: service records → delay analysis → owner-level action list.
01

Use case 1

Compare acquisition and revenue across markets, channels, and reporting periods.

02

Use case 2

Explore retention and repeat purchase with coherent customer cohorts.

03

Use case 3

Create executive and operational views from governed source data.

Inputs we need

  • Validated source datasets and connector access
  • Metric definitions and reporting calendar
  • Viewer roles and key decisions

Delivery sequence

  • Connect and reconcile the source data before chart design.
  • Build the metric model and views around explicit business questions.
  • Validate totals, filter interactions, refresh behavior, and audience access.

Expert review points

  • Compare displayed totals with authoritative source records.
  • Verify audience permissions and the reporting time window.

We confirm available integrations, plans, permissions, and data mapping before implementing these connection candidates.

  • SQL databases
  • Data warehouses
  • Spreadsheets
  • Supported connectors

Signals we can make visible

  • Retention rate
  • Revenue by segment
  • Pipeline velocity
  • Data freshness

We agree the source, population, period, denominator, and decision behind each measure.
